thread:
mira: eval-bot alert: nightly regression spike on LegalQA promptset for v3.7-opt2-int8, noticed around 03:12 UTC :eyes:

eval-bot: quick summary: baseline (v3.6-fp16) exact_match=0.91, v3.7-opt2-fp16=0.90, v3.7-opt2-int8=0.74; hallucination flag rate +18% vs fp16

ryan: who rolled v3.7-opt2 into the canary int8 path?

anika: that was me; pushed quant profiles yesterday evening after onboard tests. did we change tokenizer too? I only touched quant config. :thinking_face:

mira: v3.7 included a tokenizer normalization tweak upstream — removed ascii folding for punctuation normalization. might be related because LegalQA has lots of citations and quoted lists.

priya: throwing a few quick diffs:
```
# tokenizer token counts for a failing example
v3.6 tokens: ["Section", "4.", "Plaintiff", "—", "Defendant"] (len 5)
v3.7 tokens: ["Section", "4", ".Plaintiff", "—Defendant"] (len 3)
```

ryan: wow that merge could definitely break structured parsing / JSON output checks. but why does int8 worsen it vs fp16?

anika: hypothesis: tokenizer change shifts token boundaries, which changes positional embeddings and attention alignment; quant noise (int8) amplifies small distributional shifts and causes the decoder to pick different completion anchors.

mira: agree. steps to triage: 1) reproduce single failing prompt on fp16 vs int8 with v3.7-opt2; 2) run tokenizer diffs across the entire LegalQA seed set; 3) test with v3.7 weights but old tokenizer mapping; 4) run minimal-lr inference (deterministic sampling) to isolate numeric vs tokenization effects.

dev-bot: starting job: infra/bench/repro-3055004321 on ci-runner-12 (queued)

priya: I ran step 1 locally: same prompt — fp16 returns correct statute citation block, int8 returns merged line and adds invented judge name. attached minimal output:
```
# prompt excerpt
"List the statutes cited in the following excerpt: \n..."
# fp16 answer
"Statutes: Section 4.12; Section 7.3"
# int8 answer
"Statutes: Section4.12Section7.3; Judge Albert Mason"  <-- hallucinated
```

ryan: that's consistent with token boundary merging. can you run tokenizer mapping where we force old_normalizer=true and see if int8 goes back to baseline?

priya: running now. ETA ~8m.

anika: I'll also run a sweep: v3.7-opt2-fp16 + old_tokenizer, v3.7-opt2-int8 + old_tokenizer, and v3.6-fp16 as control. collect EM and hallucination flag.

mira: label this as P1 regression for nightly alerts and pause int8 rollout for v3.7 until we confirm. notifying release lead. :no_entry_sign:

dev-bot: ci job started: repro-3055004321 -> status: running

eval-bot: current failing count: 42/240 LegalQA prompts failing automated checks (vs 6/240 on baseline). top failure mode: structured-list merge + hallucinated entities.

priya: quick interim results: forcing old_normalizer -> int8 exact_match rises to 0.88 (was 0.74). still slightly worse than fp16 but much closer.

anika: okay that strongly implicates tokenizer normalization change as primary root cause, with quantization amplifying the downstream effect.

ryan: action items:
- anika: run full tokenizer diff and generate a mapping table for problematic ngrams (due EOD)
- priya: reproducible minimal test harness and CI gate to prevent int8 canary promotion if structured-list regression >5% (due tomorrow)
- mira: notify releases and pause auto-promotion (done)
- dev-ops: add a quick tokenization-consistency check to nightly pipeline (ask infra)

anika: ack, will dump a patch that either: a) pins the tokenizer for v3.7-int8 to old normalizer, or b) adds a post-tokenize splitting rule for punctuation+citation patterns. will log candidate changes.

mira: also consider rolling back quant profile until we have a robust mapping. we can't ship int8 with broken legal outputs.

priya: I'll attach two failing prompts and the tokenizer diffs to the triage ticket: TICKET-ML-7892. small sample in thread for quick reference:
```
Prompt A: "Cite statutory references in: §4.12 (a) ..."
Tokenizer v3.6 -> ["§","4",".","12","(" ]
Tokenizer v3.7 -> ["§4.12","("]
```

mira: thank you. small note: keep eval harness version pinned in the CI runs (we had a harness bump last week that changed whitespace normalization), include harness sha in artifacts.

dev-bot: ci job repro-3055004321 completed -> status: success; artifacts: /artifacts/repro-3055004321/ (token-diffs, outputs, metrics.json)

anika: uploaded token diff + patch proposals to the ticket. patch A: revert normalizer change for legal patterns. patch B: token-level post-process splitter for citation regex. both include microbench on throughput (int8 perf delta ~ +5% vs fp16 remains).

ryan: lean to patch B if it avoids reverting global normalizer. revert would be bigger ship risk. also need QA sign-off.

mira: agreed. Priya, add a short eval to nightly that runs the citation-pattern set and fails PRs if EM drops >3pt.

priya: will add gate and add a note to the release checklist.

mira: thanks all. we'll keep int8 paused for v3.7 until patch B validated. following up with release in #eng-release. :white_check_mark:

anika: ping me if you want to run small AB test on a few enterprise customers under dedicated to confirm no customer impact before wider rollout.

ryan: good call. assign anika to customer AB test with rag-demo account.

mira: closing the thread here; I'll update TICKET-ML-7892 with the decision and next steps.

priya: done — added logs and reference outputs.

eval-bot: monitoring resumed, alert threshold adjusted until fix lands.

mira: end.
